located in Mangalore City, Karnataka State, India. The Institute was established as Karnataka Regional Engineering College (KREC) in 1960, and upgraded as National Institute of Technology Karnataka (NITK) in 2002. Mangalore is the headquarters of the coastal district of Dakshina Kannada, and boasts an important centre of education, business and trade in the state. Sri. U. Srinivasa Mallya, a visionary and a philanthropist, contributed immensely to the development of the coastal region of Karnataka, and his effort towards establishment of KREC (now NITK) is the most significant one. In recognition of his role as the founder and architect of the institute, the campus premises is named after him as Srinivasnagar. Vision To facilitate transformation of students into good human beings, responsible citizens & competent professionals, focusing on the assimilation, generation and dissemination of knowledge. Mission Impart quality education to meet the needs of profession and society, and achieve excellence in teaching-learning and research. Attract and develop talented and committed human resources, and provide an environment conducive to innovation, creativity, team-spirit and entrepreneurial leadership. Facilitate effective interactions among faculty and students, and foster networking with alumni, industries, institutions and other stake-holders. Practice and promote high standards of professional ethics, transparency and accountability. Institute of National Importance The functioning of NITK is governed by NIT Act, 2007 and by the rules laid down by the Government of India from time to time. NITK is governed by the Board of Governors which consists of representatives of the Government of India, Government of Karnataka, Alumni, Industry and other bodies. The Chairman of the Board of Governors is nominated by the Government of India. Lush Green Campus The campus with 296 acres sets in sylvan surroundings along the coastline of Karnataka. It is a residential and self-sufficient campus equipped with all the resources. Highly Qualified Faculty Faculty members with rich academic and research experience gained from renowned indian and abroad institutes/labs strive towards imparting knowledge and honing the technical and management skills of about 6000 students. New Sports Complex with a total built-up area of 7,491 sqm inaugurated. Direct Admission of Students Abroad (DASA) coordinated. 2018 HEFA grant to strengthen Central Research Facility, and infrastructural development fund received. New academic and residential buildings about 54,840 sqm inaugurated (CSE, Chemical, Applied Mechanics, Basic Sciences, Library, Staff quarters and Girls hostel). 2017 Lecture Hall Complex with a total built-up area of about 8,193 sqm. Vertical extension of new Mechanical Engineering block (4th, 5th and 6th floors) with a total built-up area of about 6,355 sqm inaugurated. TEQIP-III commences. 2016 Centralized counselling for M.Tech/M.Arch/M. Plan (CCMT) coordinated by the Institute. Installation of total 1MWp (1000KWp) Capacity SolarPower Plants at the rooftop of 18 existing buildings on RESCO model of the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy through Solar Energy Corporation of India 2015 Mentored IIIT Dharwad entrusted by MoE. 2014 All the UG programmes got accredited for five years - Direct Admission of Students Direct Admission of Students Abroad (DASA) coordinated for five continuous years (2010-2014) 2012 New ladies hostel with 347 occupants inaugurated. 2011 New boys mega hostel with 1512 occupant inaugurated. 2010 Prepared a strategic plan for the 2010-2020. 2009 Golden Jubilee celebrations inaugurated. 2008 Recognized as major QIP centre for all PG and PhD programs. Centre of Yogic Sciences and Continuing Education opened. 2007 Designated as Institute of National Importance. Postgraduate program in ndustrial Biotechnology started. 2006 Launch of Centre of Excellence & Relevance (CORE) in Industrial Biotechnology in Chemical Engineering Department funded by TIFAC, Government of India 2004 Lead Institution status for World Bank funded Technical Education Quality Improvement Program (TEQIP) granted. 2003 First annual convocation of NITK held. 2002 Upgraded to National Institute of Technology Karnataka (NITK). 2000 Undergraduate program in Information Technology started. 2000 Lead Institution status for World Bank funded Technical Education Quality Improvement Program (TEQIP) granted. 1996 Postgraduate program in Computer Science and Engineering started. 1995 Central Computer Center established . 1994 Postgraduate program in Industrial Pollution Control started. Science and Technology Entrepreneurs Park (NITK-STEP), and Research and Development Centre for clay roofing tiles, bricks and other ceramics established. 1993 Project IMPACT funded by Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation, with World Bank and Government of India. 1992 Postgraduate program in Power and Energy Systems started. 1990 Postgraduate program in Materials Engineering started. 1988 Postgraduate program in Computer Applications started. 1985 Undergraduate program in Computer Engineering started. 1980 Affiliation changed to Mangalore University. 1971 Undergraduate program in Mining Engineering started. 1967 UN special fund and UNESCO International experts assistance in the development of postgraduate programs granted. 1966 Postgraduate programs in Industrial Structures, and Marine Structures started. 1965 Undergraduate programs in Chemical Engineering, and Materials and Metallurgical Engineering started. 1960 Founded as Karnataka Regional Engineering College (KREC) with undergraduate programs in Civil Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, and Electrical Engineering affiliated to University of Mysore. Other Activities Ranking ARIIA NIRF NITK QS Ranking Careers Teaching Positions Non-Teaching Positions Tenders How to Reach Location A lush green campus on the shores of the Arabian sea, nourished and blessed by the monsoon showers. NITK is located on the coastal belt of Karnataka, on the National Highway 66, at about 22 kms from Mangalore towards Udupi. It lies close to Mangalore International Airport, Mangalore Railway Station and the Mangalore Port. Bus Routes from Mumbai, Goa and Bangalore (that terminate at Udupi-Manipal) pass through the College and visitors can disembark right away. Accomodation All parents/ guardians with wards at NITK can apply through their wards in advance for accommodation at the International Hostel (IH) and the Institute Guest House. Besides these, Surathkal and Mangalore are dotted with a flurry of lodges, food Joints and Shopping Complexes. Get Directions Reaching NITK There are many options to travel to the campus. From Mangalore Railway Station and Bus stand All Express buses to Udupi, Manipal, Kundapur, Bhatkal or Karkala drop you at the College NITK Express Bus Stop which is closer to the Administrative Block, Departments, Girls' Hostels Block, and the Guest House. A number of Private Taxis also available at Mangalore. NITK is 21 Kms. from Mangalore on the northern side on National Highway No.66. From Surathkal Railway Station Passengers alighting at Surathkal station can engage auto rickshaws that will take them to the college 2 kms from the Station. Further, one can also reach Surathkal Bus Stand and board regular service buses that ply via the college. Other Activities Ranking ARIIA NIRF NITK QS Ranking Careers Teaching Positions Non-Teaching Positions Tenders Home > Campus Amenities NITK Campus Amenities The 295.35-acre campus caters to the needs of a comminity comprised of Faculty, Staff and Students. Staff club, shopping complex, banks with ATM facility, post office, schools, hospital, guest house, cafeterias, playground are present on the campus for the benefits of the residents. Guest Houses The Institute has four guest houses J C Bose Guest House Vikram Sarabhai Guest House Homi J Bhaba Guest House International Hostel They are located on the western side of the National Highway (NH66), near the beach (Arabian Sea). Guest House Manager Mr. Karunakar Phone : 0824-2473820, 0824-2474065 Sports Facilities A full-fledged Physical Education & Sports Department with two Students’ Activity and Sports Officers (SAS Officers) and one Assistant Physical Director provide and manage sports, games and physical fitness facilities. Infrastructure facilities are available in the sports centre for indoor and outdoor sports. In addition, a swimming pool of international standard is also available. A new and modern Sports Complex has been set up in the campus which was inaugurated by the Honorable HRD Minister. Dean(Student Affairs) Other Amenities Health Care Centre A full-fledged Health Care Centre caters to the medical and health needs of the campus residents and students with state-of-the-art facilities, ambulance support and visiting specialists. Post Office The post office in the campus caters to all the mail-related services of the residents of the institute . Shopping Centers Two shopping centers exists in the campus which include students’ and employees’ Cooperative Societies, bakery, vegetable shop, cloth shop, tailoring, saloon, beauty parlor, laundry, printing press, provisional store, among others Canteens Two canteens and four cafeterias are available. Banks Two banks (Canara bank and State bank of India) with ATM facility are available in the campus. Open Air Theatre (Students Activity Centre) One open Air theatre of about 1000 seating capacity is available. Silver Jubilee Auditorium (SJA) Auditorium of about 1,200 seating capacity is available Hostels Hostels for both boys and girls are available in the campus. The Institute being a residential campus, the majority of students (4500+) stay in hostels. There are 12 Hostel blocks for boys, 5 hostel blocks for girls with power backup. The Institute has an International Hostel too. Multiple dining halls offer a variety of cuisine for students. Reading room functions in each hostel with books and periodicals. All hostel rooms are provided with internet connection. Students actively participate in the management of hostels and dining halls. Major festivals are also celebrated in hostels. Central laundry facility is launched in the hostels from the academic year 2018-19. Student transportation facility is available from hostels to Lecture Hall Complexes/Departments and back. Institutions on Innovation Achievements (ARIIA) is an initiative of Ministry of Education (MoE), Govt. of India, to systematically rank all major higher educational institutions and universities in India on indicators related to “Innovation and Entrepreneurship Development” amongst students and faculties. ARIIA considers all major indicators which are commonly used globally to rank the most innovative educational institutions/ universities in the world. The ARIIA initiative aims to inspire Indian institutions to reorient their mind-set and build ecosystems to encourage high quality research, innovation and entrepreneurship, towards making them globally competitive, and in the forefront of innovation. NITK Surathkal has been categorized as 'Band A' institution (rank between 11-25) in category of ‘ Institute of National Importance, Central Universities & CFTIs ’ in ARIIA 2020 rankings, announced on 18th Aug 2020. Importance as per NITSER Act, 2007 of the Government of India. It is reputed for excellence in education, research, innovation and outreach activities, and is ranked among the top 20 engineering institutes of India (NIRF, 2024). Message NITK Surathkal is well-known as the institute with ‘its own’ beach, topped by a lighthouse. The NH- 66 passes between its Eastern and Western campus, connecting it to Udupi in North and Mangalore in South, passing over picturesque rivers and providing a gateway to many tourist hotspots in Western Ghats. The campus itself is lush green even in summer, and home to many birds, including peacocks. It has all basic amenities including hostels, messes, sports complex, student activity centre, health care centre, food court, shops, bank and post office. Academic and research facilities include department labs, R&D Centres of Excellence, Central Research Facility, Central Library, Central Computer Centre, Lecture Hall Complexes, Auditorium, S&T Entrepreneurs’ Park, etc. The Institute has about 300 faculty members with excellent credentials and experience, supported by about 400 staff members. There are 14 departments offering UG, PG and PhD programs, which attract the brightest students from all over India and a few from other countries. About 7000 students are presently enrolled, and nearly 2000 graduate every year. The Career Development Centre facilitates internships and placements. The Institute has over 40,000 alumni, who have excelled in different fields including academia, industry, public service, defence, media and sports. The dedicated faculty, support staff, accomplished peer students and alumni network, along with comprehensive facilities in a clean, green and well-established campus provide ample opportunities for students to explore, learn and grow into successful professionals. The Institute has set its vision of global excellence and local relevance, by integrating knowledge generation (research), dissemination (education) and application (innovation and outreach). It is continuously enhancing its academic programs, pedagogy, facilities and collaborations to meet the aspirations of the students, parents, industry and society. director@nitk.edu.in +91-824-2473000 Director's Office, 2nd Floor, Main Building, NITK Surathkal Email: director.office@nitk.edu.in E-Mail NH 66, Srinivasnagar Surathkal, Mangalore Karnataka 575025 0824 2474000 info@nitk.edu.in Our Campus Gallery Guest House (GH) Health Care Centre (HCC) Library STEP Virtual Tour Quick Links TEQIP Career Development Centre (CDC) Departments Intranet IRIS Portal Telephone Directory General Links Alumni Non Teaching Staff Recruitment REO Complaints Internal Complaints National Career Service Portal RTI Tenders and Quotations © Copyright All Rights Reserved 2026, NITK Surathkal

Information Act,2005) Proactive Disclosure under Section 4 of the RTI Act, 2005 Please see the ported Handbook shownbelow. You may also see the Old Site Link of RTI Handbook. Handbook-RTI S. No. Background of the handbook Right to information act 2005 (RTI act) 1.1 Objective purpose of this Handbook Providing information about the Institute 1.2 Users of this Handbook Students and staff of the Institute general public,etc., 1.3 Organization of the Information in this Handbook As per the guidelines of the MoE 1.4 Definitions Institute:National Institute of Technology Karnataka,Surathkal. Act:Right to Information Act,2005. MOA:Memorandum of Association between the Institute and the Ministry of HRD. 1.5 Contact Person RTI Officials 1.6 Earlier CPIO and FAAs 2.1 Vision To facilitate the transformation of students into good human beings,responsible citizens and competent professionals,focusing on assimilation,generation,and dissemination of knowledge. 2.2 Mission Impart quality education to meet the needs of profession and society,and achieve excellence in teaching-learning and research. Attract and develop talented and committed human resources,and provide an environment conducive to innovation,creativity,team-spirit and entrepreneurial leadership. Facilitate effective interactions among faculty and students,and foster networking with alumni,industries,institutions and other stakeholders. Practice and promote high standards of professional ethics,transparency,and accountability. 2.3 Brief History of the Institute National Institute of Technology Karnataka (NITK) Surathkal,formerly known as Karnataka Regional Engineering College (KREC) Surathkal,was established in the year 1960 at Srinivasnagar,Mangalore,Karnataka State. Sri U. Srinivasa Mallya,a visionary and a philanthropist was instrumental in the establishment of this Institute and hence the campus is named after him as “Srinivasnagar”. KREC made a small yet significant beginning with 3 Departments offering BE programs in Civil,Mechanical and Electrical Engineering. Since then KREC grew from strength to strength and set unprecedented records in the field of technical education in the country. Initially,the College was affiliated to the University of Mysore but in 1980 the affiliation was transferred to the Mangalore University. With every passing batch of students who went on to conquer unexplored domains in the service of humanity,the stature of KREC grew and the world recognized and applauded. So much so,‘Surathkal’is synonymous with high-quality engineering education. In 2002,the Government of India decided to grant full autonomy and accordingly the College was elevated to the status of Deemed University and renamed as the National Institute of Technology Karnataka. Subsequently,the National Institute of Technology Act,2007 was enacted by the Parliament of India to declare India’s National Institutes of Technology as Institutes of National Importance. The Act received the assent of the President of India on 5th June 2007 and became effective from August 15,2007. The Institute is governed by the rules and statutes of the NIT Act. The Institute has established itself as a premier center engaged in imparting quality technological education and providing support to research and development activities. The Institute has a long tradition of research for several decades in both traditional and modern areas of engineering and sciences in all departments. The Institute has been actively involved in applied research in looking at and resolving problems faced by the society in several areas. NITK attracts students from all over the country and abroad. NITK graduates are sought after by top industries/companies and the Institute has been rated as one of the best Institutions in the country with regard to student placements. Many of its alumni occupy coveted positions both in India and abroad and are a source of pride and inspiration to the Institute. NITK is consistently rated among the top engineering and technological institutes in India. Today,the Institute offers nine B. Tech programs,27 Post Graduate programs,and Doctoral programs in all its fourteen Departments and is making significant advances in R&D and outreach activities too. 2.4 Location The Institute is located at Srinivasnagar,Surathkal in the Dakshina Kannada District of Karnataka State,21 km. North of Mangalore city on either side of NH.66which cuts across the campus. The campus is well connected by rail,road,air and sea with the rest of the country. The airport is situated at Bajpe,20 km from Surathkal. The nearest Railway station is Surathkal (3 km.) which is on the Mangalore-Mumbai Konkan Railway route and the nearest seaport is New Mangalore which is 8 km,south of college campus. 2.5 Campus The campus covers an area of 295 acres in picturesque surroundings with Western Ghats in the East and the West Arabian Sea in the West. The campus is well laid out with roads,electrical installation,water supply,underground drainage,etc. The campus is on the seashore,is blessed with clean air and a healthy climate. The National Highway NH 66 separates the campus into the Western Side and Eastern Side campus. The Western Side of the campus houses the Departments of E&E,E&C,Computer and Information Technology,Guest Houses,STEP,Yoga center and pristine beach. 2.6 Duties of the Institute Teaching and Research. 2.7 Organisation Chart Click Here 2.8 Mechanism available for monitoring the service delivery and public grievance resolution The monitoring is done through the different Committees and the Board of Governors. 2.9 Address of the Institute National Institute of Technology Karnataka,Surathkal Srinivasnagar –575 025 Mangalore 2.10 Institute Working hours Administrative and Office Staff: 08.45 A.M. to 01.00 P. Assistance (PhD) Ph.D. Programme Doctoral programmes at NITK are offered in 14 Departments under various research areas and interdisciplinary streams, under the following categories. Full-time students on Institute Scholarship Full-time sponsored students under QIP Full-time / External Registrants - sponsored from Industry or other organizations including Educational Institutions Internal Registrants - sponsored institute of project staff of NITK 1 Full-time students on Institute Scholarship 2 Full-time sponsored students under QIP 3 Full-time / External Registrants - sponsored from Industry or other organizations including Educational Institutions 4 Internal Registrants - sponsored institute of project staff of NITK Admission to a Ph.D. Programme shall be open to Indian Nationals who passed a qualifying degree in a relevant field with a Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA) of at least 6.0 in the 0-10 scale grading system, or not less than 60% marks in the aggregate (taking into account the marks scored in all the subjects of all the public/ university examinations conducted during the entire prescribed period for the qualifying degree). However, this prescribed minimum shall be a CGPA of 5.5 or 55% marks in the aggregate for SC/ST/PwD candidates. The prescribed qualifying examination is as follows: 1 For Ph.D. in Engineering/Technology – Master’s degree in relevant field. 2 For Ph.D. in Physics – Master’s degree in relevant field 3 For Ph.D. in Chemistry - M.Sc. / M. Tech in relevant field including M. Pharma 4 For Ph.D. in Mathematics - M.Sc.in Mathematics / M. Tech in relevant field / MCA 5 For Ph.D. in Humanities, Social Science and Management – Master degree in relevant field, CA along with undergraduate degree. Only applicants having a Postgraduate Degree in Basic Sciences / Social Sciences / Humanities / Management/ Mathematics / Engineering / Technology and also have qualified through NET/GATE in-addition are eligible for admission to Ph.D. programme. Employed professionals having experience and proven competence aspiring for Ph.D. Programme will be considered under External Registration and will be allowed to pursue their research at their own location of work. Ph D Full time research scholars are eligible for a fellowship of Rs. 31,000/- pm for the first two years and Rs. 35,000/- pm for the remaining two years on satisfactory progress. Pursuant to the directives of MHRD Government of India, the revision in PhD scholarship will be effected. 165 Institute's fellowships are available at the Institute level which is flexible for department-wise allocation. The Research scholars have to assist in teaching and laboratory work assigned by the department and are eligible for 30 days’ vacation leave per year. Full-time sponsored candidates may receive complete financial support including stipend, contingency grants and project expenses from the sponsoring organizations. Internal Registrants (Institute Faculty/Staff, Project staff) are expected to work for their Ph.D. Programme while fulfilling their normal duties. External Registrants are expected to carry out their Research work in their parent organization after fulfilling certain prerequisites in the Institute. They are not entitled to Institute scholarship. The external candidate shall produce a sponsorship certificate from his employer and submit it along with the application. A minimum of one semester residential requirement is to be completed by all external registrants. External Registrants are expected to carry-out their research work in their parent organisation after fulfilling certain prerequisites in the Institute. They are not entitled for Institute scholarship. The external candidate shall produce a sponsorship certificate from his employer and submit it along with the application. A minimum of one semester residential requirement is to be completed by all external registrants. External registrants need to have an additional Research Guide from the sponsoring organisation. Full time student sponsored from Industry or other organisation are also required to produce Sponsorship Certificate. They are too not entitled for Institute scholarship. Admissions at NITK Surathkal The B.Tech. programmes at NITK Surathkal are among the most sought-after undergraduate engineering programmes in India. The Institute offers a diverse range of engineering disciplines supported by excellent academic infrastructure, research opportunities, industry collaborations, and a vibrant campus environment. The Institute offers the following B.Tech. programmes Artificial Intelligence Chemical Engineering Civil Engineering Computational and Data Science Computer Science and Engineering Electronics and Communication Engineering Electrical and Electronics Engineering Information Technology Mechanical Engineering Metallurgical and Materials Engineering Mining Engineering ADMISSION THROUGH JoSAA/ CSAB Admission to the Bachelor of Technology (B.Tech.) programmes at National Institute of Technology Karnataka (NITK) Surathkal is conducted through the Joint Entrance Examination (JEE) Main and the subsequent Joint Seat Allocation Authority (JoSAA) and Central Seat Allocation Board (CSAB) counselling processes, as prescribed by the Government of India. 1. JEE Main Examination Candidates seeking admission to the B.Tech.. Programmes at NITK Surathkal must appear for and qualify for the JEE Main examination conducted by the National Testing Agency. Candidates who qualify for JEE Main are required to participate in the JoSAA counselling process for seat allocation. 2. CSAB Special Rounds Seats remaining vacant after the completion of JoSAA rounds are offered through the CSAB Special Rounds . Eligible candidates who have not secured a seat or wish to participate in additional rounds of seat allocation may register for CSAB counselling as per the guidelines issued by CSAB. For more information, please visit the official website of JoSAA and the official website of CSAB. Seat Matrix : View the latest seat matrix on the JoSAA portal. Opening and Closing Ranks : View the opening and closing ranks of previous years on the JoSAA portal. ADMISSION THROUGH DASA Admissions to the B.Tech. programmes at NITK Surathkal are offered to eligible Foreign Nationals (FN), Overseas Citizens of India (OCI), Persons of Indian Origin (PIO), Non-Resident Indians (NRI), and Children of Indian Workers in Gulf Countries (CIWG) through the Direct Admission of Students Abroad (DASA) scheme of the Ministry of Education, Government of India. The DASA scheme provides students residing abroad with the opportunity to pursue undergraduate studies at premier technical institutions in India, including NITs, IIITs, and other Centrally Funded Technical Institutions. Admission is based on the eligibility criteria and merit as prescribed under the DASA guidelines, with JEE (Main) ranks being used for seat allocation. Candidates are advised to refer to the DASA admission portal for detailed eligibility requirements, seat matrix, fee structure, counselling schedule, and admission procedures. For more information, please visit the official website of DASA . ADMISSION THROUGH ICCR The Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR) admission route provides eligible international students with the opportunity to study at NITK Surathkal through scholarship schemes sponsored by the Government of India. ICCR, under the aegis of the Ministry of External Affairs, facilitates the admission of foreign nationals from partner countries to premier educational institutions across India. For more information about the scholarships and admission timeline, please visit the official website of ICCR Instructions for first years - B.Tech through DASA - 2026-27 Instructions for first years - B.Tech through JoSAA and CSAB- 2026-27 NH 66, Srinivasnagar Surathkal, Mangalore Karnataka 575025 0824 2474000 info@nitk.edu.in Our Campus Gallery Guest House (GH) Health Care Centre (HCC) Library STEP Virtual Tour Quick Links TEQIP Career Development Centre (CDC) Departments Intranet IRIS Portal Telephone Directory General Links Alumni Non Teaching Staff Recruitment REO Complaints Internal Complaints National Career Service Portal RTI Tenders and Quotations © Copyright All Rights Reserved 2026, NITK Surathkal

Admission Categories Regular Admissions (Through CCMT/GATE - Category A .1) Candidates with a valid GATE score can seek admission to the M.Tech programmes through the Centralized Counselling for M.Tech./M.Arch./M.Plan. (CCMT) process. Eligible candidates are entitled to receive scholarships in accordance with the norms prescribed by the Ministry of Education (MoE) for a maximum of four semesters, subject to applicable rules and regulations. Information regarding the departments, specialisations offered, eligibility criteria, and qualifying degrees is available on the CCMT portal. For more information, please visit the official CCMT portal. Seat Matrix: View the latest seat matrix on the CCMT portal . Opening and Closing Ranks: View the opening and closing ranks of previous years on the CCMT portal . Quality Improvement Programme (QIP) (Category A.2.1) Admission to M.Tech. programmes under the Quality Improvement Programme (QIP) is conducted in accordance with the guidelines prescribed by the All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE). The programme is open exclusively to sponsored permanent faculty members serving in AICTE-recognised degree or diploma institutions. Detailed information regarding eligibility, application procedures, and admission guidelines is available on the AICTE QIP Portal. Further details are available on the AICTE QIP Portal . Sponsored (Category A.2.2 ) Admission under the Sponsored Category is open to candidates who are nominated and financially supported by their employing organization. Candidates admitted under this category are not eligible for Institute scholarships. Applicants must possess a minimum of two years of full-time work experience and submit a Sponsorship-cum-Clearance Certificate in the prescribed NITK format along with the application. For more details - Admission Brochure 2026-27. Self-Financed ( Category A.2.3 ) Admission under the Self-Financed Category is open to candidates who satisfy the prescribed eligibility requirements. Candidates admitted under this category are not eligible for Institute scholarships. Selection is based on the candidate’s performance in the qualifying examination, a national-level written test, and a technical interview conducted at NITK, with appropriate weightage assigned to each component as determined by the concerned Department Postgraduate Committee (DPGC). (Research) programme provides an opportunity for academically motivated students to undertake advanced research in emerging areas of engineering, technology, and applied sciences while acquiring specialized knowledge in their chosen field. NITK Surathkal offers the following M.Tech (Research) programmes DEPARTMENT POSTGRADUATE PROGRAMMES Chemical Engineering Chemical Engineering (CG) Industrial Biotechnology (ES) Environmental Science & Technology (IB) Civil Engineering Construction Technology & Management (Includes L&T Sponsored Candidates) (CM) Environmental Engineering (EN) Geotechnical Engineering (GT) Structural Engineering (ST) Transportation Engineering (TS) Computer Science & Engineering Computer Science & Engineering (CS) Computer Science & Engineering Information Security (IS) Electrical & Electronics Engineering Power & Energy Systems (PX) Power Electronics & Control (PE&C) Power Electronics & Control for Electric Vehicle (BSGW Sponsored seats only) (PV) Electronics & Communication Engineering Communication Engineering & Networks (CN) Signal Processing & Machine Learning (SP) VLSI Design (VL) Information Technology Information Technology (IT) Mathematical & Computational Sciences Computational and Data Science (CD) Mechanical Engineering Manufacturing Engineering (MF) Mechanical Design (MD) Mechatronics Engineering (MC) Thermal Engineering (TH) Metallurgical & Materials Engineering Materials Engineering (ML) Materials Process Technology (PT) Nanotechnology (NT) Mining Engineering Rock Excavation Technology and Management (RT) Water Resources & Ocean Engineering Marine Structures (MS) Water Resources Engineering & Management (WR) Geoinformatics (GF) M.Tech. (Research) Admission Categories Regular Admissions (Category B.1) Candidates with a valid GATE score can seek admission to the M.Tech (Research) program. Selection is based on the candidate’s GATE score and performance in the qualifying examination, a national-level written test, and a technical interview conducted at NITK, with appropriate weightage assigned to each component as determined by the concerned Department Postgraduate Committee (DPGC). Eligible candidates are entitled to receive scholarships in accordance with the norms prescribed by the Ministry of Education (MoE) for a maximum of four semesters, subject to applicable rules and regulations. Sponsored (Full Time - Category B.2.1 ) Admission under the Sponsored Category is open to candidates who are nominated and financially supported by their employing organization. Candidates admitted under this category are not eligible for Institute scholarships. Applicants must possess a minimum of two years of full-time work experience in the sponsoring organization and submit a Sponsorship-cum-Clearance Certificate in the prescribed NITK format along with the application. Internal Registrants (Part Time - Category B.2.2) Candidates under this category are internal registrants who are sponsored Institute staff or project staff of NITK. Such candidates are required to submit a Sponsorship-cum-Clearance Certificate duly issued by the Director, NITK, at the time of admission. External Registrant (Part Time - Category B.2.3) Candidates under this category are sponsored by industries, educational institutions, or other organizations and are expected to carry out their research work at their parent organization after fulfilling the prescribed academic and research requirements at the Institute. Applicants must have a minimum of two years of full-time work experience in the sponsoring organization. They may also be permitted to have an additional research guide from the sponsoring organization, subject to Institute regulations. The residential requirement may be waived for such candidates, and they are expected to complete the prescribed coursework through certified courses pre-approved by the concerned Department Postgraduate Committee (DPGC). NITK are offered in 14 Departments under various research areas and interdisciplinary streams. The programme provides a rigorous academic environment that fosters innovation, critical thinking, and research excellence under the guidance of experienced faculty members. Admissions to the Ph.D. programme are offered under various scholarship and non-scholarship categories to accommodate candidates from academic institutions, research organisations, industries, and government sectors. Categories of Admission to the Ph.D. Programme Admissions to the Ph.D. programme at NITK are offered under Scholarship and Non-Scholarship categories. A. Scholarship Categories A.1 Candidates with M.E./M.Tech. or Equivalent Degree Candidates possessing an M.E./M.Tech. or equivalent degree in a relevant discipline are eligible to apply. A valid GATE score is not mandatory for this category. A.2 Candidates with B.E./B.Tech. or Equivalent Degree Candidates with B.E./B.Tech./B.Arch./B.Plan./B.Des./B.S. (four-year degree programme) in a relevant discipline may apply directly for Ph.D. admission within five years of obtaining the qualifying degree. Applicants must possess a valid GATE score. Candidates who have graduated from a Centrally Funded Institution (CFI) are exempted from the mandatory GATE requirement. A.3 Candidates with M.Sc./M.A./M.C.A./M.B.A. or Other Relevant Master’s Degree Candidates holding a Master's degree in a relevant discipline are eligible to apply. Applicants must possess a valid GATE, UGC-NET, CSIR-NET, NBHM, or DAE-JEST qualification. Candidates who have obtained their qualifying Master's degree from a Centrally Funded Technical Institution (CFTI) are exempted from this requirement. B. Non-Scholarship Categories B.1 Quality Improvement Programme (QIP) Admissions under this category are governed by the AICTE Quality Improvement Programme (QIP). Only permanent faculty members of AICTE-approved degree or diploma institutions sponsored under the QIP scheme are eligible to apply. B.2 Sponsored Candidates (Full-Time) Candidates are sponsored and financially supported by an industry, educational institution, or other recognised organisation. Applicants must have at least 2 years of continuous full-time employment with the sponsoring organisation. A sponsorship-cum-clearance certificate in the prescribed format must be submitted along with the application. B.3 Internal Registrants (Part-Time) Candidates under this category are internal registrants who are sponsored Institute staff or project staff of NITK. Such candidates are required to submit a Sponsorship-cum-Clearance Certificate duly issued by the Director, NITK, at the time of admission. B.4 Self-Financed / Non-Scholarship Candidates (Full-Time) Candidates admitted under this category are not eligible for Institute scholarship support. Admissions are made against vacant seats remaining after the sanctioned scholarship seats are filled. B.5 External Registrants (Part-Time) Candidates are sponsored by industries, educational institutions, or other organisations. Applicants must have a minimum of two years of continuous full-time work experience in the sponsoring organisation. A sponsorship-cum-clearance certificate in the prescribed format must accompany the application. Candidates are expected to carry out their research work primarily at their parent organization after satisfying the prescribed residency and coursework requirements at NITK. Such candidates may have an additional Research Guide from the sponsoring organization, and the residential requirement may be relaxed as per Institute regulations. Selection Procedure Admission to the Ph.D. programme under all scholarship and non-scholarship categories is based on performance in: A national-level written test , and A technical interview , both conducted in physical mode at NITK by the respective Departmental Research Programme Committee (DRPC). NITK Driven by a broader and better understanding of health and its impact on learning the institute has established the Health Care Centre to oversee and coordinate the medical care provided on the campus. Located within easy reach of the NITK community at the centre of the campus, opposite to the main playground, the centre plays a key role in catering to the increasing medical needs of the campus. Through the promotion of healthy lifestyles the Health Care Centre provides critical support to the academic mission. Institute Medical Officers Dr. M. L. Students may seek the advice of medical officers in selecting the hospital for admission and treatment. Pertaining to the out-patient treatment in any of the hospitals, (as referred by institute medical officers) all the bills towards medical expenses have to be submitted for reimbursement at the hostel office duly signed by the Institute Medical Officer. To support the growing population of the campus three full time Medical Officers are appointed for general consultations and treatment during the day. Visiting Consultants are available in different specialties including Allopathy, Ayurveda and Homeopathy. A full-fledged dental unit with Dental X-ray facility operates in the Health Care Centre with two visiting dental surgeons are available for consultation. Besides, night casualty operates with one medical officer and one staff nurse till midnight. Ambulance service is available 24x7 with basic facilities and a first aider. Medical Diary Medical diaries are issued at the reception counter to all the permanent employees and dependents, retired employees and the students of the institute. These medical diaries enable the doctors to maintain the medical records of the patients. Appointments are given at the reception counter in person/over telephone to consult different visiting specialists. Pharmacy The Pharmacy at the Health Care Centre is outsourced since 2007 making available all the medicines prescribed by the institute medical officers and visiting consultants free of cost. Nursing Facility Along with the regular nursing care, day care facilities like Nebulization, Oxygen Inhalation and Intravenous Fluid Infusion are available in the Heatth Centre. E.C.G. facility is also provided for the needy patients. Clinical Laboratory The basic blood, urine and stool tests are carried out in the laboratory. Investigations on blood sugar, lipid profile, blood urea and creatinine etc. are conducted using the Modern Biochemistry analyzer and blood count analyzer. Dressing Room Wound Dressing, suturing of wounds, incision and drainage procedures and other minor surgical procedures are carried out in the dressing room. Medical Facility outside campus Fourteen hospitals in Mangaluru and Udupi have been recognised by the institute for the specialized treatment in Allopathy and Ayurveda for the NITK community. Facility for Direct Payment from Institute for out-patient and in-patient treatment is made available at KMC Mangaluru. of a comminity comprised of Faculty, Staff and Students. Staff club, shopping complex, banks with ATM facility, post office, schools, hospital, guest house, cafeterias, playground are present on the campus for the benefits of the residents. Guest Houses The Institute has four guest houses J C Bose Guest House Vikram Sarabhai Guest House Homi J Bhaba Guest House International Hostel They are located on the western side of the National Highway (NH66), near the beach (Arabian Sea). Guest House Manager Mr. Karunakar Phone : 0824-2473820, 0824-2474065 Sports Facilities A full-fledged Physical Education & Sports Department with two Students’ Activity and Sports Officers (SAS Officers) and one Assistant Physical Director provide and manage sports, games and physical fitness facilities. Infrastructure facilities are available in the sports centre for indoor and outdoor sports. In addition, a swimming pool of international standard is also available. A new and modern Sports Complex has been set up in the campus which was inaugurated by the Honorable HRD Minister. Dean(Student Affairs) Other Amenities Health Care Centre A full-fledged Health Care Centre caters to the medical and health needs of the campus residents and students with state-of-the-art facilities, ambulance support and visiting specialists. Post Office The post office in the campus caters to all the mail-related services of the residents of the institute . Shopping Centers Two shopping centers exists in the campus which include students’ and employees’ Cooperative Societies, bakery, vegetable shop, cloth shop, tailoring, saloon, beauty parlor, laundry, printing press, provisional store, among others Canteens Two canteens and four cafeterias are available. Banks Two banks (Canara bank and State bank of India) with ATM facility are available in the campus. Open Air Theatre (Students Activity Centre) One open Air theatre of about 1000 seating capacity is available. Silver Jubilee Auditorium (SJA) Auditorium of about 1,200 seating capacity is available Hostels Hostels for both boys and girls are available in the campus. The Institute being a residential campus, the majority of students (4500+) stay in hostels. There are 12 Hostel blocks for boys, 5 hostel blocks for girls with power backup. The Institute has an International Hostel too. Multiple dining halls offer a variety of cuisine for students. Reading room functions in each hostel with books and periodicals. All hostel rooms are provided with internet connection. Students actively participate in the management of hostels and dining halls. Major festivals are also celebrated in hostels. Central laundry facility is launched in the hostels from the academic year 2018-19. Student transportation facility is available from hostels to Lecture Hall Complexes/Departments and back. Professor, Department of Mathematical and Computational Sciences Email: chairperson_icc-sh@nitk.edu.in Tel: 0 8 2 4 - 2 4 7 3 3 6 7 (Off) Any confidential complaints on The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace may please be mailed to chairperson_icc-sh@nitk.edu.in On August 13, 1997, the Supreme Court of India issued a landmark judgment, popularly known as Vishaka judgement that recognized and addressed sexual harassment at the workplace as a human rights violation. The Supreme court in its judgement said every women has a right to a safe workplace. The court gave directives for all employers/organizations making it mandatory to institute sexual harassment complaints committees at workplaces. The judgement also created sexual harassment prevention guidelines for the workplace. The sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act 2013 has replaced the guidelines/norms laid down by Hon' able Supreme Court on sexual harassment and came into force from December 9, 2013. The Govt. of India made rules for carrying out the provisions of this Act, 2013. In the light of enactment of The sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013, the Competent Authority has constituted an Internal Complaints Committee at NITK Surathkal(ICC-SH). The Internal Complaints Committee is responsible for Investigating every formal written complaint of sexual harassment and taking appropriate remedial measures to respond to any substantiated allegations of sexual harassment. The Internal Complaints Committee shall inquire into the complaints as per the provisions of Section 11 of the Act, 2013. During pendency of inquiries the Committee may give recommendations as may be considered necessary under the provision of Section 12 of the Act, 2013 and based on these recommendations, the Competent Authority shall take appropriate action. Policy of the Institute It is the policy of the Institute to create and maintain an environment free from sexual harassment in the Institute. The Institute strongly disapproves of any conduct that constitutes sexual harassment. All students, faculty, and staff members are advised to report any matter related to sexual harassment to the Committee against Sexual Harassment (Contact details of members are given below). All complaints will be thoroughly investigated and appropriate action will be taken promptly. The Committee will maintain confidentiality within the limits of the law and will not disclose sensitive information to any individual except for those who have a specific need to know. research as a potent form of learning by doing. Our students enrich their education through engaging in frontline, faculty-led research. Research flourishes in our fourteen departments that convene experts across disciplines to transform the cutting-edge technology in to a new horizon. The inter-disciplinary research brings the diverse talent to bear, together, on important societal problems of the country. Research at NITK is an integral part of the curriculum and a major component of the teaching-learning process. The institute takes pride in being recognized as a Centre for AICTE sponsored National Doctoral Programme and also as a Centre for Quality Improvement Programme (QIP). The newly introduced M.Tech (Research) programmes are aimed at orienting students towards novel research possibilities at an early stage. The institute assures for its scholars a broad and deep research navigation. The NITK Research Advisory Board is established to provide policy directions to research activities. The institution has attracted significant research grants from various central and state government agencies, and various industries with a total of 162 ongoing sponsored research projects. NITK has received over Rs.200 crores since 2016. A new central research facility(CRF) with a funding of Rs.80 crores from Higher Education Financing Agency (HEFA) will equip NITK with a state of the art equipment/software across departments and encourage interdisciplinary research. A Regional Academic Centre - space (RAC-s) supported by Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) will shortly been setup in NITK, to cater to the technological needs of ISRO. for Continuing Education(CCE) Objectives: The Government of India has recognized non-formal and continuing education as one of the main areas of thrust in its new educational policy. It was in this context that the Centre for Continuing Education (C.C.E) was started in the year 1987. The Centre is involved in organizing short term courses, extension courses and workshops on a wide range of topics over the years, utilizing the workforces and resources available in the institute. With the assistance of concerned departments and sponsoring agencies, the Centre has organized about 326 programmes so far, catering to the needs of working professionals from various academic institutions, government organizations, industries, commercial banks and students. The resource persons are largely drawn from NITK and at times, external faculty has also been involved. The laboratory, library and computer facilities of the institution are made available for conducting the courses. An Advisory Committee manages the CCE-NITK. This committee monitors the activities as well as the funds of the Centre. Crescendo… and the list goes on. For each season and every talent, NITK has a bunch of annual events designed to make the best of its diverse student population. Be it sports or public speaking, coding or dancing, the events aim to unveil every hidden potential . Spread across the year, these activities are not merely a break from academic life but form the essence of the NITKian tradition. Student Activities Student activities at NITK are hosted by over 25 student clubs from disciplines range across robotics, civil engineering and astronomy and to racing, film, classical arts and fashion. The clubs managed by the student representatives come together to host a range of programmes, provide organisational support to annual events and help students gain exposure to the best minds in their specific areas. Arts and Culture The NITK chapter of the Society for the Promotion of Indian Classical Music and Culture Amongst Youth (SPICMACAY) hosts programmes throughout the year. Artists of national and international acclaim are invited to give the students a glimpse of artistic brilliance in various classical arts. Bharatdarshan is another forum to help acquaint students with the diverse ethnic cultures of the country. Information Technology NITK provides 24/7 internet connectivity ( 4Gbps lease lines of 1:1) to departments, students hostels and faculty residences. The institute is equipped with 12 core single-mode fibre with 1Gbps/10Gbps backbone speed. A Central Computer Centre (CCC) with over 225 desktop PCs and 30 central servers is located at the heart of the campus. Apart from this an Image Processing lab, Information Security lab, IoT and Data Analytics lab is operative in the campus. Safety and Security Safe and secure campus with 24/7 comprehensive security and fire safety measures Dining on Campus The campus offers a variety of food services to students, faculty,staff and visitors that are open as early as 7:00am until as late as midnight. Apart from the hostel mess, two canteens and three cafeterias provide students with a variety of meal plans. Specialized health menus are among the among the highlights of our hostel cuisine. Athletics The institute is equipped with diverse resources to maintain the physical wellness of the student community. A full-fledged Sports Complex was set up in the campus earlier this year to encourage athletics. The Physical Education & Sports Department comprising of two Students’ Activity and Sports Officers (SAS Officers) and one Assistant Physical Director support and manage sports, games and physical fitness activities. New and modern infrastructure facilities are installed at the Sports Complex for indoor and outdoor games. Health and Wellness The Health Care Centre functioning on the campus provides comprehensive medical care to the resident population. The students can avail the health services throughout the week. The centre is dedicated to promote and sustain student health by providing free consultation, medicines, weekly visits by specialists and ambulance support. leadership of a President, supported by a Vice-President, Secretaries, and a Joint Secretary. The Council serves for a full academic year and is further strengthened by several dedicated support committees : Alumni & Placement Committee, Academic Activity Committee, Health & Wellness Committee, Sports Committee, Incident Committee (for Cultural fest), Engineer Committee (for Technical fest), Incub8 Committee(Entrepreneur & business fest). These committees collaborate closely with the central Council to organize events, represent student interests, and enhance campus life through targeted initiatives. “Lead with Values, Rise with Bharat” The mandate of the Students’ Council is to coordinate and regulate all aspects of student life at NITK. The Students’ Council, in collaboration with institute stakeholders, strives to create a vibrant and progressive student environment through the following objectives: To actively encourage and support a wide range of student-led academic, cultural, and extracurricular initiatives that contribute to holistic development. To nurture leadership, teamwork, and organizational competencies among students by facilitating structured opportunities for engagement and responsibility. To provide a constructive platform for identifying student concerns and encouraging open, solution-oriented dialogue through regular interaction forums. To cultivate an informed, responsible, and participative student community, while promoting values of inclusivity, social awareness, and mutual respect. To streamline administrative and logistical processes for recognized student activities, ensuring smooth coordination for events, venues, and resources. To maintain a collaborative channel of communication between students and the institute, ensuring that student perspectives are appropriately represented in relevant discussions. To align student aspirations with the broader goals of the institute, working towards academic excellence, campus well-being, and community engagement. To promote a positive, proactive, and solution-driven student culture by supporting initiatives in innovation, sustainability, and student welfare. Structure The President, Vice President, General Secretary, Joint Secretary, PG Secretary, Ph.D Secretary, Alumni & Placement Committee(APC), Academic Activity Committee(AAC), Health & Wellness Committee(HWC), Sports Committee, Hostel Council, Engineer, Incub8, Incident, and all elected Class Representatives and Nominated Persons shall together be known as the NITK Students’ Council. The Students’ Council Core led by the President supported by a Vice-President, General Secretary , Joint Secretary , PG & Ph.D Secretaries. The basic outline and structure is as follows: Vision We look forward to upholding the core pillars of Initiative, Engagement, Transparency, Accountability, and Communication throughout the year — ensuring that every action of the Students’ Council reflects purpose, responsibility, and service. The Students’ Council has been and will continue to be instrumental in fulfilling Vision 2026, and we urge every student of this prestigious institution to actively participate, contribute, and engage in shaping a stronger student community. We envision a vibrant and value-driven student leadership at NITK — one that leads with integrity, fosters unity through a shared vision, and empowers every student to rise as a contributor to the progress of Bharat. Our goal is to cultivate a campus culture where academic excellence, moral responsibility, and national consciousness move hand in hand — preparing future leaders who think beyond themselves and act for society and the nation. international technical societies have set up local student chapters at NITK. They include Indian Society for Technical Education (ISTE), the Institution of Engineers, the Computer Society of India, the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) and Robotics Club NITK. The Society of Automotive Engineers (SAE) has an active chapter constituted by Mechanical Engineering students. They conduct events like 'How stuff works', 'Under the hood', 'Can you fix it?' and also a Vintage Auto Expo. NITK has a racing team which participates in SAE BAJA. In 2011, its sister team NITKRacing participated in FSAE Michigan USA 2011, the toughest circuit on the FSAE calendar. It was the only team from India to participate in the event. NITK has a Linux Users Group, which along with the WEB Enthusiasts Club promotes FOSS and Linux. The Robotics Club (along with IEEE) at NITK is a group of students that aims to create a robotics culture in the institute. They provide tools, equipment and expert guidance so that academic projects in the area of robotics can be successful. The Engineers' Forum for Entrepreneurship Awareness (E-FOREA) encourages entrepreneurial ideas from students and promotes leadership and entrepreneurship on campus. E-Pitch is their flagship business idea competition which attracts participation from all over the country. The amateur astronomy Star Gazing Club conducts star-watching shows for the students and faculty. It runs astronomy workshops for school students in the region. It has recently acquired a radio telescope setup from Radio Jove, and this affords the students some opportunities in learning astronomy beyond the visible spectrum. The Robotics Club of NITK is a group of hobby robot enthusiasts. Members involve in presenting seminars on various levels of robotics to participating in renowned tech-fests like TECHFEST, IITB, SHAASTRA, IITM,etc.Recently, it has undertaken to build the Coconut Harvester Robot, in joint with CPCRI, Kasaragod to build an autonomous coconut tree harvester. CULTURAL CLUBS The Rotaract Club conducts social, cultural and technical events for the students and club members alike. These include blood donation camps, cloth donation drives, coastal clean-up camps, and events conducted by the National Service Scheme (NSS) chapter of NITK. The Mangalore chapter of the Society for Promotion of Indian Classical Music and Culture Among Youth (SPICMACAY) is centred at NITK and is one of the biggest chapters in the country. It organises concerts and lectures by maestros of Indian classical art forms and strives to raise awareness of Indian culture in the surrounding regions through lectures, orientations and conventions. The chapter celebrated its Silver Jubilee by hosting the 27th Annual National Convention of SPICMACAY from 28 May to 3 June 2012. Literary, Stage and Debating Society (LSD) is the apex literary forum of the institute. The club mainly conducts quizzes while also holding debates and organising plays. LSD was formed in 2004 from the quiz club to cater to literary events other than quizzes. LSD is one of the best quiz clubs in India, having produced quizzers who have won competitions nationwide. Members of the club also contribute to the NITK Quiz blog, which has been active since 2008. Dance Dramatics and Fashion Club (DDFC) organises 'Spandan' annually, which provides students a platform to showcase their talent at dance and theatre. The NITK Music Club organises music shows generally called Musical Night and play popular music at the outdoor auditoriums. A variety of styles are on display at these events, from Indian classical music to fusion to rock. The NITK Films Club screens movies at the Student's Activity Centre every Friday during the semester. Apart from English and Hindi releases, regional films are shown as well. The Press Club brings out a fortnightly wall magazine News Wagon, providing a tongue-in-cheek look at life around the campus, besides bringing out the official yearbook,The Vitruvian VOICE (Vedic Oasis for Inspiration, Culture and Education) is a youth group run by the students, for the students. Using the principles present in the ancient Vedic scriptures, they train students in a blend of character and competence. The NITK Photography Club captures photos and videos of events happening at NITK. It conducts "Expose", which is a national level photography contest organised yearly during Incident. The club contributes to the official yearbook, The Vitruvian. The Vitruvian has got a rebirth in the year 2013-14 and came out with the new version The Shoreline with vital and profound changes. service program conducted by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports of the Government of India. Popularly known as NSS, the scheme was launched in Gandhiji's Centenary year, 1969. Aimed at developing student's personality through community service, NSS is a voluntary association of young people in Colleges, Universities and at +2 level working for a campus-community linkage. NSS at NITK NSS NITK established in the year 2017 as a Self-Financed Unit Recognized by the Regional Directorate of NSS, Bengaluru. About 100 Volunteers are participating in this noble cause at present. Students from 1st year and 2nd year are joining this voluntary movement and rendering their services time to time to the society. Engr Coy NCC, NITK Surathkal) About 2 Kar Engr Coy NCC 2 Kar Engr Coy NCC is located at NITK Surathkal since it's inception in 1963. It was almost started in parallel with the institute. NCC welcomes you to a new world of patriotism, discipline, adventure, courage and work ethics. It is important to remember that becoming a good NCC cadet is not an easy task. A lot of hard work and dedication is required to achieve such a goal. Here, in NCC, we teach you to be a good leader, a decision maker, a good team member, and above all, to be a disciplined citizen. NCC has very close associations with the armed forces. Ours is the ARMY wing of NCC . Enrolment into NCC starts as soon as you enter into the college in the first year. A cadet has to be in NCC for 3 years in order to get his/her B-certificate and C-certificate. Cadets will be given free uniform, shoes and other dress material by NCC and cadets have to maintain the same till they complete their training. As per the new policy, Cadets are awarded B-certificate, after they complete their second-year training, followed by 'B' certificate examination and C-certificate in their third-year training, followed by 'C' certificate examination. Exam includes both practical and theory papers. They also need to undergo at least one camp of 10 days duration, each year, prior to their respective examinations. C-certificate holds very special importance in all walks of life, including in PLACEMENTS . Cadets will have to attend the NCC classes regularly on Saturday mornings, which includes PT, Drill, Weapon training and other theory classes. Twice a year there will be Firing . In the class, cadets are taught interesting subjects like map reading, various types of weapon training, Mines etc. There will be regular parades, in which cadets are taught marching skills. Discipline is given the highest priority. This is what distinguishes NCC cadet from other students. Cadets voluntarily participate in various social service activities like Swachh Bharath, Coastal Cleaning, Disaster Management, Blood Donation camps etc. Cadets actively participate in Independence Day and Republic Day Parades on 15th August and 26th January, respectively. 'To be in NCC, is to experience how to live a life less ordinary.' and Families" WELFARE MEASURES AGAINST DISCRIMINATION AND RAGGING NITK Surathkal doesn’t believe any type of discriminations viz. gender, caste, creed and dogmas etc. Everybody is considers to be on the equal forefront. We never encourage and support any such socially harmful activities. Gender wise everybody gets equal chance to showcase their talents and expertise in respect of students and staff. Caste and religion bar is not practiced in the institute premises in any means. NITK Surathkal has not been encountered with any major ragging activity till date but still we deal with strict measures to any type of ragging activities reported upon. NITK Surathkal runs its anti-ragging policy with the following measures: We have an independent Anti ragging cell with committee members consisting with the faculty, staff members, students and local police. All the members formulate certain rules and regulations and laid down the measures to curb the ragging across the campus. A special anti-ragging squad is formulated every year during the starting of the academic year who goes on round across the departments and hostels at different times and check for any untoward happenings. A group of 10 members (faculty & staff) used to be on duty for 6 hrs and then changes to another group which goes 24 hourly basis for the first 2 months continuously. Apart from these all the wardens are always vigilant across the hostels to look after the activities and also the security personals are deputed to all the hostels blocks and all the corners across the campus. Anti-ragging posters citing all types of harassment and their repercussion and the disciplinary actions against that etc. are displayed across the campus in various locations including departments, hostels, cafeterias, staircases, play grounds, stalls, and all other major establishments identified wherever students movements are frequent and chances of untoward activity is more. Moreover as per the directives from UGC and AICTE about the anti-ragging affidavits to be submitted by the admitted students and their parents as well, NITK Surathkal strictly adhere to that and collect the affidavits during the student’s registration time at the institute. Time and again the institute also organize workshop and expert talks on ragging and other unethical activities among the student fraternity. Nationally at IIM MATRIx 2026 Home > MME Students team Named Among the Top 10 Nationally at IIM MATRIx 2026 NITK Surathkal Students Named Among the Top 10 Nationally at IIM MATRIx 2026 Startup Hackathon, Organised by the Indian Institute of Metals at IIT Hyderabad: NITK is proud to share that a team of students from the Department of Metallurgical and Materials Engineering — Shubhang S. Galagali, Anindith B. L., Suhas Gowda M, and U. M. Tejasvi Karanth — guided by Prof. Subray R. Hegde and Dr. Sumanth Govindarajan, has been named among the Top 10 teams at IIM MATRIx 2026. Notably, theirs was the only shortlisted team to represent an NIT. IIM MATRIx (Materials Research, Innovation & Entrepreneurship Expo) is a national startup hackathon organised by the Indian Institute of Metals in the domains of Metallurgical/Materials and Manufacturing/Production Engineering. Held at IIT Hyderabad on 19 June 2026, 25 shortlisted teams demonstrated their working prototypes before a panel of experts, industry leaders, and investors, with seed grants of up to ₹20 lakh on offer to support promising innovations. The team's innovation, AI-FA (AI-Assisted Failure Analysis), is an AI copilot for industrial failure investigation, which grew out of the team's capstone project under the same faculty guidance. Grounded in real on-site failure investigations at nearby industries — where the team contributed to formal investigation reports — AI-FA tackles a persistent industrial gap: failure investigation remains a largely manual, expert-dependent task, with AI yet to play a meaningful role. AI-FA turns the evidence of a failed component into a first-pass root-cause assessment in minutes rather than weeks— helping industries learn from every failure, big or small, as early movers driving the shift from a human-centric Industry 5.0 toward the AI-driven factories of Industry 6.0. This achievement reflects the team's ability to combine metallurgical domain knowledge with modern artificial intelligence to build a practical, real-world solution for industry. The team is now working to take AI-FA forward as a startup. Congratulations to the team for their dedication, innovation, and problem-solving, and sincere thanks to the faculty and mentors who supported them throughout this journey. Engineering Thought Leaders Home > Sreevalsa Among 50 Influential Global Civil Engineering Thought Leaders Dr. Sreevalsa Among 50 Influential Global Civil Engineering Thought Leaders Dr. Sreevalsa Kolathayar, Associate Professor, Department of Civil Engineering, National Institute of Technology Karnataka (NITK) Surathkal, has been featured in the prestigious global list of “50 Influential Thought Leaders in Civil Engineering – 2026” curated by Jonno White (Australia), a globally recognised leadership consultant, author, and host of the Leadership Conversations Podcast. The recognition places Dr. Sreevalsa Kolathayar among leading international experts and practitioners shaping the future of civil engineering across areas such as climate resilience, sustainable infrastructure, transportation, water systems, disaster risk reduction, digital transformation, and geotechnical engineering. Importantly, NITK Surathkal and IIT Delhi are the only two Indian institutions represented in this global Top 50 list. In introducing the list, Jonno White highlighted the critical role of civil engineering in shaping human existence, stating that every road, bridge, tunnel, levee, water main, and stormwater system reflects civil engineering decisions that directly influence society and communities. He further noted that while civil engineers profoundly shape the modern world, many of the profession’s most important thinkers remain among the least visible public intellectuals globally. The list was curated not as a compilation of historical personalities, but as a recognition of “living voices actively building the profession’s next chapter.” The selection deliberately moved beyond commonly featured names and focused on professionals across six continents who are actively publishing, researching, speaking, mentoring, advocating, and influencing the future direction of civil engineering practice and policy. Dr. Sreevalsa Kolathayar has been featured under Category 4: “Water, Environment and Climate Resilience” for his contributions in earthquake geotechnical engineering, disaster risk reduction, liquefaction hazard assessment, landslide studies, and sustainable infrastructure research. He has been listed together with globally recognised experts including Pedro J.J. Alvarez (Rice University, USA), Costa Samaras (Carnegie Mellon University and former White House OSTP Advisor), Dipak Gyawali (Nepal Water Conservation Foundation), Paul Chinowsky (University of Colorado Boulder), Dr Priya Parikh (Imperial College London), Jayantha Obeysekera (Florida International University), and Arthur Antoine. The article also acknowledges Dr. Kolathayar’s active engagement in international research collaborations, conferences, and dissemination of innovative engineering solutions related to sustainability and resilience. His work particularly addresses the challenges faced by rapidly urbanising and hazard-prone regions, with emphasis on resilience-oriented engineering solutions for complex geological and climatic conditions. This recognition reflects the growing global visibility of NITK Surathkal’s contributions to advanced research and innovation in sustainable civil engineering. No. 227CV012) in the Department of Civil Engineering (Geotechnical Engineering), National Institute of Technology Karnataka (NITK), Surathkal, has been selected to participate in a reputed international scientific conference with financial support recommended by the Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF) , Government of India. to 6 th February, 2026. We are pleased to share that all our teams performed exceptionally well in the tournament, achieving the following commendable results: Women’s Teams Chess: 3 rd Place (Bronze) Athletics : 3 rd Place Overall (Bronze) Men’s Teams Athletics : Overall Champion (Gold) Chess: 2 nd Place (Silver) Total Medal tally in Athletics: Category Gold Silver Bronze Men 4 1 6 Women 0 4 4 Total 4 5 10 In addition, the following players excelled in their respective individual categories: In Women’s Athletics, Ms. Jeeva K V (Mechanical Engineering) secured two Silver medals in the 100 m and 4×100 m relay, and two Bronze medals in the 200 m and 4×400 m relay. In Men’s Athletics, Mr. Akhil Banoth (Mechanical Engineering) secured three Gold medals in the 200 m, 400 m, and 4×100 m relay, and one Bronze medal in the 4×400 m relay. Mr. Rohit V. (Ph.D., Physics) participated in the Hammer Throw event and threw an impressive 41.60 metres , winning the Gold medal . He was also crowned the “Most Powerful Man” of the All India Inter NIT Athletics Meet . In Women’s Chess, Ms. Vinitha M. Rao (Mechanical Engineering) , Captain of the Girls’ Chess Team, secured the Silver medal on the 3rd Board . In Men’s Chess, Mr. Aaron Sanju Thomas (Artificial Intelligence) secured the Gold medal on the 1 st Board , and Mr. Ekansh Goel (Information Technology) secured the Silver medal on the 2 nd Board . The Director, Deputy Director, Registrar, Office of the Dean (Student Welfare), all Deans, SAS Officers , and the entire NITK community extend their heartfelt congratulations to all the participants for their outstanding performance, dedication, and for bringing laurels to the Institute. Meet 2025–26 held at NIT Delhi Home > Results of the All India Inter NIT Sports Meet 2025–26 held at NIT Delhi The results of the All India Inter NIT Sports Meet 2025–26 for Kabaddi, Power Sports and Tug of War (Men & Women), held at NIT Delhi from 21st to 23rd December 2025. Total 26 NITs participated in the tournament along with IIEST Shibpur. our teams performed exceptionally well in the tournament, achieving the following : Men’s Team: Kabaddi : Champion (1st place) Gold medal In an impressive display of skill and determination, Mr. Veerendra M from the Kabaddi team earned the title of Most Valuable Player of the Tournament. Also Nunawat Sravan from the Kabaddi team was crowned as the Best Defender of the Tournament. Tug of War : 3rd Place (Bronze) Power Sports : Weight Lifting: Overall 3rd Place Under 61 Kg: Shankar Gowda (Gold Medal) Under 73 Kg: Kirti Jai (Bronze Medal) Under 89 Kg: Yaadram Meena (Gold Medal) Bodybuilding: (Best Physique) Under 60kg category Tanishq gold medal Abishith bronze medal Under 70kg category, Hema swaroop : Silver medal Under 75kg category Thushar bali : Bronze medal Under 85kg category Hitesh dagar. Gold medal Under 90kg category Thanish. Gold medal Champion of The Champion : Hitesh dagar Women's Team: Kabaddi : 3rd Place (Bronze Medal) The Director, Deputy Director, Registrar, Office of the Dean (Student Welfare), all Deans, SAS Officers , and the entire NITK community extend their heartfelt congratulations to all the participants for their outstanding performance, dedication, and for bringing laurels to the Institute. photos NH 66, Srinivasnagar Surathkal, Mangalore Karnataka 575025 0824 2474000 info@nitk.edu.in Our Campus Gallery Guest House (GH) Health Care Centre (HCC) Library STEP Virtual Tour Quick Links TEQIP Career Development Centre (CDC) Departments Intranet IRIS Portal Telephone Directory General Links Alumni Non Teaching Staff Recruitment REO Complaints Internal Complaints National Career Service Portal RTI Tenders and Quotations © Copyright All Rights Reserved 2026, NITK Surathkal
